title: Zero-Downtime Column Rename and Type Migration in 24/7 Production
realWorldScenario: A core table `orders` (100 million rows, 3,000 writes/sec) has a column `amount INT` storing dollars that must be converted to `amount_cents BIGINT` to support multi-currency fractional cents. A naive `ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN amount TYPE BIGINT;` will lock the table for 45 minutes.
questionStatement: Design a comprehensive zero-downtime database migration pattern to migrate `amount` to `amount_cents BIGINT` without locking concurrent writes or disrupting older application versions. Detail the expand-and-contract (dual-write) pattern with views, triggers, batch backfills, and final cleanup.
expectedConcepts: Dual-write trigger to synchronize live writes during transition
Keyset batch backfill with pause to prevent lock and WAL saturation
NOT VALID check constraint followed by VALIDATE CONSTRAINT
Zero application downtime and rollback capability
hints: Why does ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN TYPE lock the entire table and rewrite all rows?
How does a dual-write trigger allow old and new code to run simultaneously?
How do you backfill 100 million rows without blowing up WAL or holding row locks?
